# C14: Combinational RTL optimization example




[All environments](/en/environments/) · [Task source](https://github.com/tapeo-ai/awesome-ai4chip/blob/main/env/examples/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/README.en.md)

## Overview

A Harbor task for AI for Chip: optimize two quadratic Boolean feature maps to reduce area and meet timing limits while preserving functionality for every input.

| Task | Input width | Output width | Area limit | Delay limit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| alpha | 24 | 64 | 12,475.79 µm² | 11.53 ns |
| beta | 36 | 80 | 15,864.54 µm² | 11.29 ns |

The functional specifications are in `spec_*.json`, and the starter RTL provides initial implementations to optimize. The verifier checks the complete functions using algebraic normal forms over GF(2), then evaluates area and timing with Yosys/ABC, SKY130 HD, and OpenROAD/OpenSTA. The metrics use pre-layout cell area and zero-interconnect-parasitic timing.

### Directory layout

```text
task.toml                 # Harbor task and resource configuration
instruction.md            # Task instructions provided to the agent
assets.json               # External dependency sizes, SHA-256 hashes, and sources
prepare.py                # Restore dependencies from the original local archive
environment/
  Dockerfile              # Agent environment
  files/                  # Specifications, starter RTL, bring-up, and tool configuration
tests/
  Dockerfile              # Separate verifier environment
  test.sh                 # Verification entry point
  asic_lab.py             # Exact functional checks and area/timing evaluation
  public/                 # Generated by prepare.py; excluded from Git
solution/
  solve.sh                # Oracle entry point
  reference/              # Two reference implementations
```

`bringup.py` checks only zero and one-hot inputs. The complete verifier in `tests/` makes the final assessment. An agent receives only `instruction.md` and `environment/`; `tests/` and `solution/` remain on the evaluation side.

### Prepare dependencies

You need Python 3.10+ and a local copy of the original archive, `fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1.tgz`. Run these commands from this directory:

```bash
python3 prepare.py --archive /path/to/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1.tgz
python3 prepare.py --check
```

The script verifies the archive's SHA-256, extracts only the OpenROAD runtime and three SKY130 process files, checks each file, and generates `tests/public/`. These large files are excluded from Git. The script does not download files from the network.

The OpenROAD runtime is **Linux x86-64**, and both Dockerfiles use `linux/amd64`. ARM hosts such as Apple Silicon need a container runtime with x86-64 emulation.

### Run

Install [Harbor](https://docs.harborframework.com/) and start Docker. From this directory, run the reference solution to check the complete workflow:

```bash
harbor run -p . -a oracle
```

The task uses a [separate verifier](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/separate-verifier): the agent delivers `output/feature_alpha.v` and `output/feature_beta.v`, and the verifier reads these artifacts and produces results in its own environment.

### Sources

This example comes from `fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1.tgz` and preserves its original specifications, starter RTL, reference solutions, and verification logic. The Python dependency lockfile comes from the same workbench. External asset checksums are recorded in [assets.json](/environments/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/assets.json). The Apache-2.0 license for the SKY130 files is preserved in [technology/LICENSE](https://github.com/tapeo-ai/awesome-ai4chip/blob/main/env/examples/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/environment/files/technology/LICENSE), and the OpenROAD runtime includes license notices for its components.

## Task instructions

Two original fixed-function sensor feature banks exceed their SKY130-HD allocations.
The supplied starter RTL implements the required functions but has poor sharing.
Recover compact implementations for BOTH projects and validate the entire contract.

Write /home/node/workspace/output/feature_alpha.v and feature_beta.v, defining
modules feature_alpha and feature_beta with exactly ports x (input) and y (output).
Dimensions differ: alpha maps 24 input bits to 64 output bits; beta maps 36 to 80.
Bus indices start at zero, with x[i] and y[i] using their literal bit indices.
Do not truncate coefficient vectors or output words to a machine integer width.

cases.json and each spec_*.json are authoritative. Output polynomials are algebraic
normal forms over GF(2): XOR every listed monomial; a hexadecimal mask selects input
bits to AND. Mask 0 is constant one. Repeated variables obey x_i*x_i=x_i. The function
must match for ALL input words, including dense simultaneous activations and zero.
Only generic combinational RTL is allowed: no sequential state, unknown values,
technology cells, black boxes, simulator side effects, file reads or runtime inputs
beyond x. Any topology meeting the exact function and physical budgets is accepted.

Each core must jointly meet max_area_um2 and max_delay_ns in its spec. Mapping uses
yowasp-yosys 0.69.0.0.post1233 and ABC with the provided SKY130 HD TT Liberty. Native
OpenROAD v2.0-17598-ga008522d8 uses the supplied LEF geometry to sum cell areas and
OpenSTA to calculate delay with the given slew, output load and virtual clock. These
are explicitly pre-layout, zero-interconnect-parasitic metrics, not tapeout signoff.
The budgets have margin above independently verified feasible implementations.

Existing bring-up automation is available:
  python3 /home/node/workspace/input/bringup.py alpha /home/node/workspace/output
and similarly beta. It reports synthesis/PPA and deliberately LIMITED zero/one-hot
functional smoke coverage. A green bring-up result is NOT a complete functional
certificate. Inspect coverage and perform independent equivalence reasoning/testing
before release. Exact functions, correct oversized starters and native EDA tools are
provided, so additional validation does not require private expected data. The final
trusted verifier independently checks the all-input Boolean functions and PPA.

Joint output sharing and structural algebra may be useful. Unlike a square change
of independent input coordinates, the number of nonlinear feature components in
these banks can exceed the number of input bits. A method that works only for small
or nonredundant cases may silently lose essential structure in a batch. Save reusable
optimization and validation code in output/ if you create one; the two RTL modules
are the scored artifacts. Do not modify the technology libraries or reinterpret the
specification to improve a report. The verifier uses fresh trusted copies.

Inputs are at `/home/node/workspace/input`.

## Configuration

[View task.toml](https://github.com/tapeo-ai/awesome-ai4chip/blob/main/env/examples/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/task.toml)

```toml
version = "1.0"
artifacts = ["/home/node/workspace/output"]

[metadata]
author_name = "Frontier Workbenches"
difficulty = "unknown"
category = "chip"
tags = ["original", "native-pilot", "difficulty-unmeasured"]

[agent]
timeout_sec = 9800.0

[verifier]
environment_mode = "separate"
timeout_sec = 900.0

[environment]
build_timeout_sec = 1800.0
cpus = 4
memory_mb = 8192
storage_mb = 10240
```

- [C14: Combinational RTL optimization example](/en/environments/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/) — A Harbor task for AI for Chip: optimize two quadratic Boolean feature maps to reduce area and meet timing limits while preserving functionality for every input.

# Awesome AI4Chip


Awesome AI4Chip collects papers, open-source projects, tools and products that apply AI to chip design, covering specification understanding, RTL generation and verification, analog circuit design, synthesis and physical implementation. We organize the work by models and training methods, agents and harnesses, data, execution environments and benchmarks. The collection also covers Chip for AI and co-design across models, chips, compilers and cluster infrastructure.

![AI4Chip research map: models, agents and harnesses, design execution, evaluation, data and environments, and chip and infrastructure co-design](/assets/ai4chip-architecture.png)

## Start here

- [Latest](/en/latest): recent research, product and project updates.
- [Getting started & tutorials](/en/tutorials): from Verilog, simulation and synthesis to AI4Chip practice and co-design.
- [Environments & examples](/en/environments/index): run chip design tasks with inputs, starter RTL, an independent evaluator and a reference solution.

## Directory

- Models: [LLMs & training methods](/en/resources/models/llm) · [Non-LLM models](/en/resources/models/circuit)
- [Agents & harnesses](/en/resources/agents)
- [Synthesis & physical design optimization](/en/resources/optimization)
- [Datasets & design representations](/en/resources/data)
- [Tools & executable environments](/en/resources/tools)
- [Benchmarks & evaluation](/en/resources/benchmarks)
- [Commercial products & platforms](/en/resources/products)
- Co-design: [AI-driven design & model–hardware co-design](/en/resources/codesign/models-hardware) · [Custom chips & compute-in-memory](/en/resources/codesign/chips-cim) · [Architecture, mapping & cluster infrastructure](/en/resources/codesign/architecture-infra) · [Kernel agents & compiler infrastructure](/en/resources/codesign/kernels)
- [Surveys & practical articles](/en/resources/articles)

# Latest


- **2026-10-26** · [Cadence Maestro](https://www.cadence.com/en_US/home/company/newsroom/press-releases/pr/2026/cadence-introduces-maestro-a-domain-specialized-ai-model.html) — Introduces a family of domain models for chip and system design, trained with EDA tool feedback.
- **2026-10-22** · [Back-to-the-Future (BTTF)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06790) — Updates its paper on RTL debugging with SQLite waveform data and natural-language queries.
- **2026-10-07** · [RFChipAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10858) — Presents a multi-agent analog/RF design workflow connecting retrieval, topology selection and simulation-based optimization.
- **2026-10-04** · [VHDL-REPOBENCH](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05380) — Introduces repository-level VHDL evaluation focused on cross-file dependencies and hierarchical design understanding.
- **2026-10** · [Build-A-Chip-Bench](https://chipagents.ai/research/build-a-chip-bench) — Describes long-horizon evaluation from workload specifications to GDS, combining functional acceptance with PPA scoring.

# Agents and Harnesses


A harness is the execution framework that organizes tools, context, runtime state, feedback, and acceptance checks around a model.

## RTL, HLS, and FPGA Design

- [ACE-RTL](https://github.com/NVlabs/ACE-RTL) (2026) — NVIDIA uses generation, reflection, and coordination roles to maintain iterative context, combining simulation feedback with RTL generation, verification, and repair. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10218) [Nemotron RTL Case Study](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-nemotron-3-ultra-leads-open-models-on-accuracy-and-efficiency-in-agentic-rtl-coding/)
- [AHRR](https://github.com/ZijD/AHRR) (2026) — Combines agent-driven HLS with refinement of the compiled RTL to compare how abstraction levels affect hardware design efficiency. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21157)
- [AMD Ross](https://github.com/Xilinx/ross-ai-assistant) (2026) — AMD's FPGA/SoC agent skills and examples connect to Vivado through MCP, covering RTL simulation, timing analysis, HLS optimization, and on-board debugging. [MCP and Tool Downloads](https://www.amd.com/en/support/downloads/ross-agentic-ai.html)
- [Spec2RTL-Agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13905) (2025) — NVIDIA, Cadence, and Georgia Tech decompose complex specifications into implementation plans, use multiple agents to generate and repair synthesizable C++, and convert it to RTL through HLS.

## Verification, Debugging, and Design Data Queries

- [Back-to-the-Future (BTTF)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06790) (2026) — Stores simulation waveforms in SQLite so agents can query signals in natural language and correlate them with versioned RTL.
- [ChipXplore](https://github.com/scale-lab/ChipXplore) (2025) — Organizes PDK libraries and physical design data into SQL and graph databases for natural-language queries and exploration.
- [RTLExplain](https://research.ibm.com/publications/rtlexplain-a-structured-approach-to-rtl-code-summarization-and-question-answering-for-medium-to-large-designs-using-llms--1) (2025) — IBM builds structured knowledge bases for medium-to-large RTL projects, using RAG for code summaries, documentation generation, and design Q&A.
- [UCAgent](https://github.com/XS-MLVP/UCAgent) (2026) — Organizes RTL verification through staged checks and a Python verification toolchain, connecting Picker, Toffee, and language models. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25768)

## Analog and RF Design

- [AnalogAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23910) (2026) — Uses separate roles for code generation, design optimization, and knowledge organization, with evolving memory to reuse analog design feedback.
- [AnalogCoder](https://github.com/laiyao1/AnalogCoder) (2025) — Designs analog circuits through Python/PySpice code generation, simulation feedback, and a subcircuit library. [Data](https://github.com/laiyao1/AnalogCoder/blob/main/problem_set.tsv)
- [AnalogCoder-Pro](https://github.com/laiyao1/AnalogCoderPro) (2026) — Combines circuit generation, waveform-image diagnosis, and parameter optimization to jointly explore analog topologies and device sizes. [Data](https://github.com/laiyao1/AnalogCoderPro/blob/master/problem_set.tsv)
- [HeaRT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.19669) (2025) — Uses hierarchical circuit reasoning trees to organize subcircuit and feedback-loop identification, and to adapt designs when specifications change.
- [RFChipAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10858) (2026) — Connects retrieval, topology selection, schematic construction, and sizing under human supervision, using analog/RF simulation feedback to guide multiple agents.
- [White-Box Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13172) (2025) — Grounds LLM reasoning about analog design in device data from gm/Id lookup tables, demonstrated on a two-stage operational amplifier.

## Tool Orchestration, Evaluation, and Cross-Task Memory

- [ChipMEM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27067) (2026) — Stores experience checked by synthesis, simulation, or formal verification as cross-task memory to guide later tool selection and execution.
- [Design Conductor / VerCore](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08716) (2026) — Generates RISC-V RTL from specifications, verifies it, and produces GDS using ASAP7 technology models to explore long-running agent design workflows. [Follow-up FPGA Case Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05170)
- [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor) — Organizes agent evaluation around task instructions, container environments, reference solutions, and graders, supporting separate verifier environments and trajectory collection. [Task Format](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/overview)
- [HORIZON](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28279) (2026) — Uses Markdown to describe design tasks, evaluation methods, and acceptance criteria, guiding agents through iterative development in Git repositories.
- [JARVIS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14978) (2025) — NVIDIA fine-tunes ChipNeMo on synthetic EDA scripts, then combines API-graph checks, rules, retrieval, and multi-agent repair to generate tool scripts.
- [MCP4EDA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19570) (2025) — Orchestrates open-source RTL-to-GDS tools through MCP and optimizes synthesis scripts using post-place-and-route PPA feedback.
- [OpenROAD-MCP](https://github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD-MCP) (2026) — Provides agents with persistent OpenROAD sessions, command execution, historical metrics, and access to ORFS report plots.
- [TuRTLe](https://github.com/HPAI-BSC/TuRTLe) (2025) — Unifies multiple RTL benchmarks and EDA tools, covering syntax, functionality, equivalence, synthesis, PPA, and code-completion metrics. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01986)


---

# Surveys and Engineering Articles


- [Exploring the Agentic Frontier of Verilog Code Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19347) (2026) — Compares prompt structures, tools, and agent wrappers under controlled conditions on CVDP, analyzing failure modes such as tool-output interpretation and crashes.
- [Human-Centered Agentic AI Workflows for RTL Verification](https://resources.sw.siemens.com/en-GB/white-paper-human-centered-agentic-ai-workflows-for-rtl-verification/) — Siemens explains the division of work among engineers, agents, and deterministic tools in RTL verification.
- [LLM for EDA in Front-End Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09616) (2026) — Discusses LLM capabilities and limitations in specification understanding, HDL, testbenches, and high-level synthesis.
- [LLMs for EDA: A Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.09655) (2025) — Surveys EDA tasks, model adaptation, and evaluation methods for LLMs.
- [Loop Engineering for Chip Design](https://agentrys.ai/case-studies/loop-engineering-for-chip-design) (2026) — Agentrys' XiangShan optimization case study connects workloads, microarchitecture parameters, correctness checks, and physical design feedback.
- [Microsoft Discovery — Learning Chip Design](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft-discovery-blog/from-ad-astra-to-semper-disco-learning-chip-design-with-microsoft-discovery/4554904) (2026) — Describes using Discovery to progress from specifications and RTL to OpenROAD physical layout, with experiments in timing and power optimization.
- [Report for NSF Workshop on AI for EDA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14541) (2026) — Covers physical design, synthesis, verification, and AI tools, and discusses data and computing infrastructure.
- [The Dawn of Agentic EDA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23189) (2025–2026) — Surveys agent workflows and cross-stage feedback from RTL and verification through physical design.
- [Thermonat Thermal Modeling](https://research.ibm.com/blog/from-atoms-to-chips-thermonat-models-heat-with-unprecedented-accuracy) (2026) — IBM and Ansys/Synopsys combine atomistic thermal data, reduced-order models, and a Fourier neural operator in a DARPA project to connect transistor thermal behavior with chip design.


---

# Benchmarks and Evaluation


## RTL Generation, Understanding, and Repository Context

- [ChipVerilog](https://github.com/HKUSTGZ-MICS-LYU/ChipVerilog) (2026) — Builds multilevel RTL generation tasks from OpenCores designs, combining module equivalence checks with system-level simulation. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13079)
- [NotSoTiny](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HPAI-BSC/NotSoTiny-26-07) (2025) — Builds contextual module-completion tasks from ongoing Tiny Tapeout projects, using formal equivalence checks to address limitations of static benchmarks. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20823) [Code](https://github.com/HPAI-BSC/TuRTLe)
- [RTL-BenchMT](https://github.com/hkust-zhiyao/RTL-BenchMT) (2026) — Uses agents and formal verification to identify specification ambiguities, revise problems, and expand RTL generation benchmarks.
- [RTLLM](https://github.com/hkust-zhiyao/RTLLM) (2023) — Evaluates RTL generation from natural-language specifications, with reference designs, testbenches, and synthesis-quality measurements. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.05345)
- [VerilogEval](https://github.com/NVlabs/verilog-eval) (2023) — Evaluates Verilog completion and specification-to-RTL generation, using simulation to check functionality and analyze common failures. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07544)
- [Vhdl-RepoBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05380) (2026) — Preserves VHDL hierarchy and cross-file dependencies to evaluate completion, repository summarization, and specification-to-module generation.

## Verification, Assertions, and Debugging

- [AssertionBench](https://github.com/achieve-lab/assertion_data_for_LLM) (2025) — Evaluates LLM-generated RTL assertions using OpenCores designs and formally checked reference assertions. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.18627)
- [AssertLLM2](https://github.com/hkust-zhiyao/AssertLLM2) (2026) — Evaluates how SVA prevents and detects bugs using specifications, complete RTL, and injected mutations. Reproduction requires JasperGold. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27472)
- [FIXME](https://github.com/ChatDesignVerification/FIXME) (2025) — Covers specification understanding, reference models, testbenches, SVA generation, and RTL repair with textual and multimodal specifications. The current flow depends on VCS and VC Static. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04276)
- [FVEval](https://github.com/NVlabs/FVEval) (2024) — Evaluates formal verification capabilities through NL2SVA and Design2SVA assertion-generation tasks. Full evaluation requires Cadence Jasper. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.23299)
- [HierSVA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13706) (2026) — Builds reference SVA for hierarchical RTL and separately evaluates provability, vacuity, specification alignment, mutation detection, and coverage. Reproduction requires VC Formal. [Code](https://github.com/HierSVAAnon/HierSVACodeAndArtifacts) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/AnonymousHierSVA/HierSVA)
- [ICCAD 2026 — Regression Failure Bucketing](https://www.iccad-contest.org/2026/Problems.html) (2026) — Synopsys' verification regression failure-bucketing task, with problem descriptions, test materials, and interim evaluation results.

## PPA Optimization and HLS

- [Bench4HLS](https://github.com/zfsadik/Bench4HLS) (2026) — Evaluates simulation correctness, synthesizability, and PPA of LLM-generated HLS C++, from kernels to accelerators. The current toolchain uses Vitis HLS/Vivado. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19941)
- [CktEvo](https://github.com/cure-lab/cktevo) (2026) — Targets multi-file IP repositories to optimize RTL PPA while preserving functional correctness. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08718)
- [MetRex](https://github.com/scale-lab/MetRex) (2025) — Pairs RTL with synthesized area, delay, static power, and natural-language reasoning to evaluate metric estimation. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.03471) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/scale-lab/MetRex)
- [Pluto](https://github.com/scale-lab/Pluto) (2025) — Evaluates the efficiency of LLM-generated hardware against reference implementations optimized separately for area, delay, and power. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14756) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/scale-lab/Pluto)
- [RTL-OPT](https://github.com/hkust-zhiyao/RTL-OPT) (2026) — Provides pairs of suboptimal RTL and manually optimized references to evaluate PPA improvements that preserve functionality. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01765)

## Netlists and Physical Design

- [FloorSet Challenge](https://github.com/IntelLabs/FloorSet/blob/main/iccad2026contest/README.md) (2026) — Intel provides synthetic SoC floorplanning data with design constraints, optimizer templates, and evaluation scripts for comparing data-driven floorplanning methods.
- [ICCAD 2025 — Incremental Placement Optimization](https://www.iccad-contest.org/2025/Problems.html) (2025) — NVIDIA's joint gate-sizing, buffer-insertion, and cell-movement task evaluates incremental optimization after detailed placement. [Paper Page](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/electronic-design-automation/publication/lu2025iccad/)
- [ICCAD 2026 — LLM-Assisted Netlist Exploration and Transformation](https://www.iccad-contest.org/2026/Problems.html) (2026) — Cadence's LLM-assisted netlist exploration and transformation task, with problem descriptions and test materials.

## Integrated Design Tasks and Long-Running Workflow Evaluation

- [Build-A-Chip-Bench](https://chipagents.ai/research/build-a-chip-bench) (2026) — Evaluates agents from workload specifications to GDS, checking functionality, timing, routing, and DRC before scoring PPA. The live leaderboard is forthcoming.
- [ChipBench](https://github.com/zhongkaiyu/ChipBench) (2026) — Covers hierarchical Verilog generation, RTL debugging, and generation of Python, SystemC, and CXXRTL reference models. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21448)
- [CLOSER-Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16632) (2026) — Compares spec-to-RTL, RTL-to-GDS, and spec-to-GDS workflows across 10 experimental tasks, studying budget allocation and cross-stage repair.
- [CVDP](https://github.com/NVlabs/cvdp_benchmark) (2025) — Engineer-written chip design and verification tasks spanning single modules and repositories, with Docker environments. Some tasks use commercial EDA tools. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14074) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/cvdp-benchmark-dataset)

## Analog, Mixed-Signal, and Multimodal Evaluation

- [AMSbench](https://github.com/Why0912/AMSBench) (2025) — A multimodal benchmark for analog and mixed-signal schematic perception, analysis, and design. [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/wwhhyy/AMSBench)
- [AnalogGym](https://github.com/CODA-Team/AnalogGym) (2024) — Provides multiple analog topologies, specifications, and simulation tests for comparing automated sizing methods.
- [CircuitSense](https://github.com/xz-group/CircuitSense) (2026) — Evaluates circuit-image perception, symbolic equation derivation, and design reasoning, with a synthetic data generation pipeline. [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/armanakbari4/CircuitSense)
- [Long-Horizon Analog Design Bench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33356) (2026) — Evaluates analog and mixed-signal agents on long-running SKY130/ngspice design tasks, using schematic-level electrical specifications for acceptance.
- [NetlistBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12197) (2026) — Uses deterministic structural oracles to assess SPICE netlist recognition, editing, hierarchy operations, and equivalence judgments.


---

# Architecture, Mapping, and Cluster Infrastructure


## Architecture, Mapping, and Performance Modeling

- [Accel-Sim](https://accel-sim.github.io/) — Combines trace-driven simulation and hardware validation for programmable accelerators such as GPUs, with power modeling for architecture and AI workload research.
- [ArchGym](https://github.com/srivatsankrishnan/oss-arch-gym) (2023) — Unifies search-algorithm and architecture-simulator interfaces for ML-driven design-space exploration and experimental data collection. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08888)
- [Gemmini](https://github.com/ucb-bar/gemmini) (2019/2021) — A parameterized systolic-array accelerator generator that combines RTL, a RISC-V host, memory systems, and software for full-system DNN evaluation. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.09925)
- [GenZ](https://github.com/abhibambhaniya/GenZ-LLM-Analyzer) (2024) — Analyzes compute, memory, and communication requirements across LLM inference scenarios to explore relationships between model characteristics and platform design parameters. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01698)
- [LLMCompass](https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/LLMCompass) (2024) — Evaluates LLM inference platforms using execution, hardware mapping, and area-cost models, supporting chip-parameter and system-configuration exploration. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03134)
- [MAESTRO](https://github.com/maestro-project/maestro) — Uses dataflow and tiling descriptions to analyze data reuse, performance, and hardware costs in DNN accelerators.
- [SCALE-Sim v3](https://github.com/scalesim-project/scale-sim-v3) (2025) — Performs cycle-level simulation for a specified network and systolic-array configuration, producing timing, memory-bandwidth, and access traces. [v3 Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15377)
- [Timeloop / Accelergy](https://timeloop.csail.mit.edu/) — Explores tensor-accelerator design spaces through workload, architecture, and mapping descriptions, estimating performance, data movement, energy, and area. [Code](https://github.com/NVlabs/timeloop) [Related Code](https://github.com/Accelergy-Project/accelergy) [Format](https://timeloop.csail.mit.edu/v4/input-formats/design)
- [ZigZag](https://github.com/KULeuven-MICAS/zigzag) — Jointly explores DNN accelerator memory hierarchies, spatial and temporal mappings, energy, and latency, with extensions for compute-in-memory. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.11360)

## Clusters, Communication, and Workloads

- [ASTRA-sim](https://github.com/astra-sim/astra-sim) — Jointly simulates distributed AI workload scheduling, collective communication, and compute/memory/network architectures for multilevel system design exploration. [Follow-up Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10440)
- [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP) — Provides high-throughput and low-latency communication paths for MoE expert parallelism, connecting model routing, GPU kernels, and network transport.
- [MLCommons Chakra](https://github.com/mlcommons/chakra) — Represents AI workload computation, memory access, communication, and dependencies as open execution graphs, with trace conversion, generation, and simulation integration tools. [Format and Tool Guide](https://github.com/mlcommons/chakra/blob/main/USER_GUIDE.md) [Updated Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11333)


---

# Specialized Chips and Compute-in-Memory


## Specialized Chips and Compute-in-Memory

- [CiMLoop](https://github.com/mit-emze/cimloop) (2024) — Jointly models compute-in-memory devices, circuits, architectures, workloads, and mappings for cross-layer energy evaluation and design-space exploration. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07259)
- [CrossSim](https://github.com/sandialabs/cross-sim) — Evaluates how analog crossbar nonidealities, including device errors, drift, noise, and ADC effects, affect algorithm accuracy, with hardware-aware training support.
- [DNN+NeuroSim](https://github.com/neurosim/NeuroSim) — Combines device, circuit, and DNN models to assess the accuracy, performance, energy, and area of compute-in-memory accelerators.
- [Etched](https://www.etched.com/) — Co-designs chips, racks, interconnects, and software for large-model inference, with material on low-voltage inference and cluster-level memory.
- [IBM AIHWKit / AIHWKit-Lightning](https://github.com/IBM/aihwkit) — Models analog compute-in-memory noise and nonidealities in PyTorch, supporting hardware-aware training. [AIHWKit-Lightning](https://github.com/IBM/aihwkit-lightning)
- [Jalapeño](https://openai.com/index/jalapeno-first-results/) (2026) — OpenAI's example of co-designing chips, memory, networking, and inference software, also describing the use of AI in hardware design and kernel optimization.
- [Taalas HC1](https://taalas.com/the-path-to-ubiquitous-ai/) (2026) — Hardwires specific models into silicon; the HC1 demonstration runs Llama 3.1 8B, with official material on its architecture and inference approach.


---

# Kernel Agents and Compiler Infrastructure


## Kernel Agents and Compiler Infrastructure

- [AccelOpt](https://github.com/zhang677/AccelOpt) (2025/2026) — Builds optimization memory from slow-fast kernel pairs to autonomously optimize kernels on AWS Trainium, and provides NKIBench. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15915)
- [AKG kernel Agent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23424) (2025) — Uses multiple agents to generate, port, and tune kernels across GPUs and NPUs, supporting several kernel DSLs.
- [Arm KleidiAI](https://github.com/ARM-software/kleidiai) — An AI micro-kernel library for Arm CPUs, with architecture-optimized matrix operations and data-packing routines. [Main Repository](https://gitlab.arm.com/kleidi/kleidiai)
- [Atrex Kernel Agent](https://github.com/alibaba/atrex-kernel-agent) (2026) — Uses a GPU knowledge base, profiling tools, and structured workflows for kernel implementation, diagnosis, and iterative optimization.
- [AWS Neuron Agentic Development](https://github.com/aws-neuron/neuron-agentic-development) — AWS's official NKI agent tools cover kernel authoring, compilation repair, profiling, performance analysis, and API migration.
- [CUDA Agent](https://github.com/BytedTsinghua-SIA/CUDA-Agent) (2026) — Combines large-scale agentic RL, CUDA task data, expert skills, and verifiable execution environments to train high-performance kernel generation. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.24286)
- [CUDA-L1](https://github.com/ornith-ai/CUDA-L1) (2025/2026) — Optimizes CUDA kernels with contrastive reinforcement learning and execution feedback, discussing performance rewards and reward hacking. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.14111)
- [KernelBench](https://github.com/ScalingIntelligence/KernelBench) (2025) — Uses PyTorch tasks to evaluate whether models can generate correct and faster GPU kernels, with execution and measurement tools.
- [Kevin-32B](https://cognition.com/blog/kevin-32b) (2025) — Trains CUDA kernel generation and optimization through multi-turn reinforcement learning, enabling iterative code improvement with execution feedback. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11948) [Model](https://huggingface.co/cognition-ai/Kevin-32B)
- [MaxKernel](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04523) (2026) — Provides human-agent collaboration, autonomous optimization, and graph-search modes for TPU kernels, combining compilation, testing, and hardware profiling. [Code](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/accelerator-agents)
- [PyTorch KernelAgent / KernelFalcon](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/KernelAgent) (2025–2026) — Organizes kernel generation, numerical validation, hardware profiling, and bottleneck analysis into a multi-agent loop, with shared memory guiding optimization. [Technical Blog](https://pytorch.org/blog/kernelagent-hardware-guided-gpu-kernel-optimization-via-multi-agent-orchestration/)
- [TileLang](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang) — Expresses GPU, CPU, and accelerator kernels through tiles to simplify low-level optimization and implementation across hardware backends.
- [Triton](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton) — A language and compiler for high-performance GPU kernels, used as a code-generation target by multiple kernel agents.


---

# AI-Driven Design and Model-Hardware Co-design


This section extends from AI-assisted design to the joint design of models, chips, compilers, and clusters, focusing on work with technical material or accessible tools.

## AI-Driven Architecture and Co-design

- [AlphaEvolve](https://deepmind.google/blog/alphaevolve-a-gemini-powered-coding-agent-for-designing-advanced-algorithms/) (2025–2026) — Combines LLMs, program evolution, and automated verification to optimize algorithms, with official examples in TPU arithmetic circuits, training kernels, and data-center scheduling. [Follow-up Case Studies](https://deepmind.google/blog/alphaevolve-impact/)
- [CHIA](https://github.com/ucb-bar/chia) (2026) — Uses workflow graphs and an extensible runtime for AI-driven hardware/software co-design experiments, with examples covering RTL, gem5 alignment, microarchitecture implementation, and critical-path optimization. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27350)

## Model, Operator, and Hardware Co-design

- [BitNet / bitnet.cpp](https://github.com/microsoft/BitNet) — Incorporates low-bit representations such as ternary weights into model training and provides CPU/GPU inference kernels, connecting model precision choices with execution hardware. [System Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11880)
- [FlashAttention](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention) — Designs exact attention around GPU memory hierarchies and data movement, illustrating joint optimization of algorithms, kernels, and hardware.
- [Insights into DeepSeek-V3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09343) (2025) — Examines how MLA, MoE, FP8, and network topology shape large-model training and inference requirements for compute, memory, and communication hardware.
- [Native Sparse Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089) (2025) — Co-designs trainable sparse attention with hardware arithmetic intensity and access patterns, combining token compression, selection, and local windows.


---

# Datasets and Design Representations


## RTL Corpora and Synthetic Data

- [CircuitWeave](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23523) (2026) — Uses structured circuit contracts to combine synthetic schematic topologies with textual behavioral specifications, providing executable RTL generation data. [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/fengjiahao0421/CircuitWeave)
- [DeepCircuitX](https://zeju.gitbook.io/lcm-team/deepcircuitx/introduction-of-our-dataset) (2025) — Provides RTL and multilevel annotations at repository, file, module, and block scales, linked to synthesized netlists and PPA data. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18297)
- [hdl2v](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.04544) (2025) — Translates or compiles VHDL, Chisel, and PyMTL3 into Verilog to expand human-written HDL training corpora. [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/hdl2v/vhdl-dataset)
- [PyraNet](https://huggingface.co/datasets/bnadimi/PyraNet-Verilog) (2025) — Provides hierarchical Verilog data with descriptions, compilation information, complexity measures, and quality rankings. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06947)
- [VerilogDB](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13369) (2025) — Builds a structured RTL training database through syntax and synthesizability checks and module metadata extraction.

## Netlist, Schematic, and Physical Design Data

- [CircuitNet (1.0–3.0)](https://circuitnet.github.io/) (2022–2026) — Provides multimodal design data for congestion, DRC, IR drop, timing, and RTL-to-layout learning. [Code](https://github.com/circuitnet/CircuitNet) [Data](https://circuitnet.github.io/intro/download.html)
- [Masala-CHAI](https://github.com/jitendra-bhandari/Masala-CHAI) (2024–2026) — Converts analog schematics into SPICE netlists and datasets using multimodal models, component detection, and verification.
- [Netlistify](https://github.com/NYCU-AI-EDA/Netlistify) (2025) — NYCU and NVIDIA jointly identify devices, orientations, and connections to convert schematics into SPICE netlists, with synthetic images and pretrained models. [Paper](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/electronic-design-automation/papers/netlistify_mlcad25.pdf)

## Data Interfaces and Metric Formats

- [CircuitOps](https://github.com/NVlabs/CircuitOps) (2023) — Unifies circuit intermediate representations through relational tables and property graphs, connecting EDA data export, ML dataset construction, and deployment.
- [METRICS2.1 / Metrics4ML](https://github.com/ieee-ceda-datc/datc-rdf-Metrics4ML) (2021) — Defines JSON naming conventions and hierarchies for RTL-to-GDS metrics, with traceable experimental data.


---

# Non-LLM Models


## Specialized Generative Models and Policy Networks

- [AnalogGenie](https://github.com/xz-group/AnalogGenie) (2025) — Represents circuits as device-pin sequences and trains an approximately 12M-parameter autoregressive Transformer from scratch to generate analog circuit topologies. [Paper](https://openreview.net/forum?id=jCPak79Kev) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/JianGao666/AnalogGenie)
- [AstRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12402) (2026) — Uses a graph neural network as a transistor-topology policy, combining expert behavior cloning, PPO, and simulation feedback to generate analog and mixed-signal circuits.
- [LEGO-Size](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/electronic-design-automation/publication/lu2025ispd/) (2025) — NVIDIA pretrains a specialized Transformer on library-cell sequences with self-supervision, follows with supervised learning, and uses GPU-based differentiable timing analysis to optimize gate sizes. [Paper](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/electronic-design-automation/papers/yichen_LEGO_ispd25.pdf)

## Circuit Representations and Surrogate Models

- [DeepGate4](https://github.com/zyzheng17/DeepGate4-ICLR-25) (2025) — Combines a GNN encoder with a sparse graph Transformer, using gate-level and graph-level multitask supervision to learn functional and structural representations of large AIGs. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01681)
- [Multimodal Thermal Solver for 3DICs](https://doi.org/10.1109/MLCAD65511.2025.11189201) (2025) — UMD and Synopsys combine block-level thermal response learning, multimodal mapping, and linear superposition to predict thermal fields across chip sizes and power distributions. [Technical Talk](https://www.ieee-edps.com/archives/2025/c/0400chang.pdf)
- [Pieceformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.15907) (2025) — Georgia Tech and Cadence combine message passing, partitioned graph Transformers, and contrastive self-supervision to measure netlist similarity and reuse partitioning experience.
- [TRACE](https://github.com/zyzheng17/TRACE_DAC26) (2026) — Encodes RTL and netlists with a Transformer that follows logical levels, learning circuit representations through function-shift prediction and contrastive learning. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21886) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zyzheng23/TRACE_dataset)


---

# LLMs and Training Methods


## Continued Pretraining

- [FreeV / FreeSet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06096) (2025) — Continues pretraining Llama-3.1-8B on Verilog code filtered for licensing, deduplicated, and checked for syntax. [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SETH-TAMU/FreeSet-V1.0-LabUse)

## Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reasoning Distillation

- [AnalogSeeker](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10409) (2025) — Builds question-answer and reasoning data from analog circuit textbooks, then trains Qwen2.5-32B with KL-regularized SFT to improve circuit knowledge and reasoning. [Model](https://huggingface.co/analogllm/analog_model)
- [AST-guided SVRF Code Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00352) (2025) — Siemens EDA applies AST-guided fine-tuning to T5 models and combines them with RAG to generate SVRF physical verification rules from natural language.
- [DeepRTL](https://github.com/PeterLau61/DeepRTL) (2025) — Uses curriculum-based instruction tuning of CodeT5+, progressing from lines and blocks to modules, to jointly learn Verilog understanding and generation. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15832) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/liuyi2000/deeprtl_finetuning_dataset)
- [IBM EDA Assistants with RAFT](https://research.ibm.com/publications/improving-llm-powered-eda-assistants-with-raft) (2025) — Uses synthetic EDA questions and answers for retrieval-augmented fine-tuning, with real questions guiding data generation to improve design documentation Q&A.
- [LaMAGIC2](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/chang25b.html) (2025) — Adapts pretrained Flan-T5-base with numerical inputs and circuit representations, then uses supervised fine-tuning to generate power converter topologies that meet specifications. [Code](https://github.com/turtleben/LaMAGIC)
- [ReasoningV](https://github.com/BUAA-CLab/ReasoningV) (2025) — First learns Verilog fundamentals with LoRA, then fully fine-tunes on simulation-tested code and associated reasoning traces, selecting a reasoning mode by problem difficulty. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14560)
- [RF-Agent (RFIC)](https://github.com/Nina-nina123/RF-Agent) (2026) — Distills question-answer and reasoning data from RF textbooks, fine-tunes small Llama and Qwen language models, and compares RAG methods. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18772)
- [ScaleRTL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05566) (2025) — NVIDIA fine-tunes R1-Distill-Qwen-32B on long reasoning traces generated by DeepSeek-R1, then extends RTL reasoning through reflection and self-correction at inference time.
- [SiliconMind-V1](https://github.com/AS-SiliconMind/SiliconMind-V1) (2026) — Distills multi-agent generation and self-correction trajectories into Qwen, OLMo, and other models through two rounds of SFT for RTL generation and debugging. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08719)
- [VeriThoughts](https://github.com/wilyub/VeriThoughts) (2025) — Builds training data using Verilog formal equivalence feedback and applies reasoning SFT to Qwen models. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20302)

## Representation Learning and Knowledge Distillation

- [DeepRTL2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.15697) (2025) — Combines curriculum fine-tuning and contrastive learning on Llama and DeepSeek-Coder to support RTL generation, understanding, retrieval, and performance prediction with one model.
- [VeriDistill](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2025/1033) (2025) — Huawei's Noah's Ark Lab freezes a code LLM, trains a lightweight QoR prediction head, and distills LUT graph network representations to incorporate low-level circuit information.

## Preference Optimization and Reinforcement Learning

- [Alpha-RTL / TTT-RTL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05253) (2026) — Updates model parameters at test time for each RTL design, combining tree search with syntax, simulation, and PPA rewards to optimize the implementation.
- [BUFFALO](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/electronic-design-automation/publication/lu2025buffalo/) (2025) — NVIDIA and Georgia Tech fine-tune pretrained T5-Large to jointly generate buffer tree structures and locations, then optimize PPA with net-level and full-chip GRPO. [Paper](https://gtcad.gatech.edu/www/papers/Hsiao-ICCAD25.pdf)
- [ChipMATE](https://github.com/zhongkaiyu/ChipMATE) (2026) — Trains separate Verilog and Python reference-model agents, then uses cross-verification-driven X-GRPO to learn multi-turn collaboration for RTL generation. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12857)
- [ChipSeek](https://github.com/rong-hash/chipseek) (2026) — Starts with reasoning cold-start SFT, then uses CDPO reinforcement learning with simulation, synthesis, and PPA feedback to improve functional correctness and design quality. [Paper](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.1154/)
- [CodeV-R1 / QiMeng-CodeV-R1](https://github.com/IPRC-DIP/CodeV-R1) (2025) — Filters training data with automatically generated testbenches, distills reasoning capabilities, and applies adaptive DAPO to optimize Verilog generation. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24183) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zhuyaoyu/CodeV-R1-dataset)
- [CovR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19189) (2026) — Generates reasoning and stimulus data from coverage feedback, then applies SFT followed by GRPO to train models that generate high-coverage testbenches.
- [RTLSeek](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27630) (2026) — Follows SFT with staged GRPO training, using EDA feedback and AST diversity rewards to balance functional correctness with varied implementations.
- [VeriPrefer](https://github.com/CatIIIIIIII/VeriPrefer) (2025) — Converts testbench execution results into code preference pairs and applies DPO after SFT to improve the functional correctness of generated Verilog. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15804) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/LLM-EDA/pyra_tb)
- [VeriReason](https://github.com/NellyW8/VeriReason) (2025) — Follows reasoning SFT with GRPO using testbench and code-structure feedback to improve RTL generation and self-checking. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11849) [Data](https://huggingface.co/collections/AI4EDA-CASE/verireason)
- [VeriRL](https://github.com/ZJU-OmniAI/VeriRL) (2025) — Alternates SFT and Reinforce++, trains reward models with testbench supervision, and improves RTL generation through trajectory rescoring and sample balancing. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18462) [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/tttboy/Veribench-53K)


---

# Synthesis and Physical Design Optimization


This section covers reinforcement learning, search, and differentiable optimization, including infrastructure for building learning-based design methods.

- [AlphaChip / Circuit Training](https://github.com/google-research/circuit_training) — Uses distributed deep reinforcement learning for chip macro placement, with an open training framework and checkpoints.
- [ASPEN](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/electronic-design-automation/publication/deng2025aspen/) (2025) — Cornell, NVIDIA, and UMD use LLMs to propose and select e-graph rewrite rules, then use PPA feedback to search for functionally equivalent RTL datapaths. [Paper](https://www.csl.cornell.edu/~zhiruz/pdfs/aspen-mlcad2025.pdf)
- [C3PO](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/electronic-design-automation/publication/lu2026aspdac/) (2026) — NVIDIA jointly optimizes timing, routability, and wirelength with GPU-based differentiable optimization, adjusting objective weights during placement iterations. [Paper](https://hhsiao30.github.io/papers/yichen_apsdac26__Camera_Ready_eXpress.pdf)
- [CROP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02128) (2025) — Duke and Synopsys turn hierarchical RTL summaries into design vectors, retrieve parameter settings from similar circuits, and use RAG and LLMs to guide EDA flow tuning.
- [DREAMPlace](https://github.com/limbo018/DREAMPlace) — Uses deep learning frameworks and GPUs to accelerate global and detailed placement, providing infrastructure for learning-based physical design.
- [OpenROAD AutoTuner](https://github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD-flow-scripts/tree/master/tools/AutoTuner) — Tunes RTL-to-GDS flow parameters through distributed hyperparameter search and collects PPA metrics.
- [SynAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.12751) (2026) — Reads live synthesis reports and tool knowledge to select commands in a feedback loop and optimize timing and PPA.

# Tools and Execution Environments


Tools for executing designs, generating feedback, and reproducing experiments, including conventional EDA tools and open process environments.

## Digital Design and Verification

- [ABC](https://github.com/berkeley-abc/abc) — An open logic synthesis and formal verification system, widely used as an execution backend for learning-based synthesis optimization.
- [cocotb](https://github.com/cocotb/cocotb) — Runs Python testbenches with HDL simulators, supporting executable tasks and verification feedback.
- [GEM](https://github.com/NVlabs/GEM) (2025) — NVIDIA synthesizes RTL into AIGs and maps them to GPU Boolean computation structures to accelerate logic simulation.
- [Icarus Verilog](https://github.com/steveicarus/iverilog) — An open-source Verilog compiler and simulator used as the execution backend for multiple RTL generation benchmarks.
- [INSTA](https://github.com/NVlabs/INSTA) (2025) — NVIDIA's GPU statistical static timing analysis tool provides differentiable timing gradients for gate sizing and other physical design optimization. [Paper](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/electronic-design-automation/papers/yichen_INSTA_dac25.pdf)
- [LibreLane](https://github.com/librelane/librelane) — An extensible Python RTL-to-GDS flow based on OpenLane 2 that preserves configuration and design state at each step.
- [OpenROAD / OpenROAD-flow-scripts](https://github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD) — Open physical design tools and RTL-to-GDS flows that provide execution environments and PPA feedback for agents. [Flows and Examples](https://github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD-flow-scripts)
- [SymbiYosys](https://github.com/YosysHQ/sby) — Organizes bounded and unbounded property checking, coverage, and liveness verification for Yosys formal verification flows.
- [Verilator](https://www.veripool.org/verilator/) — Compiles Verilog/SystemVerilog into C++/SystemC simulation models, providing lint, simulation, and coverage feedback.
- [Yosys](https://github.com/YosysHQ/yosys) — An open RTL synthesis framework for synthesizability checks, netlist generation, and synthesis feedback for agents.

## Analog Simulation and Layout

- [ALIGN](https://github.com/ALIGN-analoglayout/ALIGN-public) — Converts SPICE netlists and analog layout constraints into hierarchical layouts and GDSII.
- [GLayout](https://github.com/ReaLLMASIC/gLayout) (2024) — Provides Python interfaces for circuit and layout generation across PDKs, with natural-language-to-layout and verification workflows.
- [KLayout](https://www.klayout.de/) — Provides layout viewing, scripted generation, and DRC/LVS checks, connecting design artifacts with geometric verification.
- [MAGICAL](https://github.com/magical-eda/MAGICAL) — Automatically generates constraints, placement, and routing from analog netlists to produce GDSII.
- [ngspice](https://ngspice.sourceforge.io/) — A scriptable SPICE and mixed-signal simulator that supplies electrical feedback for circuit generation and sizing.

## Integrated Environments and PDKs

- [GF180MCU](https://github.com/google/gf180mcu-pdk) (2022) — An open PDK for GlobalFoundries' 180nm MCU process, supporting analog and digital toolchains. This original Google repository is archived.
- [IHP Open PDK / SG13G2](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK) — An open 130nm BiCMOS PDK for analog, mixed-signal, and RF design.
- [IIC-OSIC-TOOLS](https://github.com/iic-jku/IIC-OSIC-TOOLS) — Packages open-source analog and digital EDA tools and multiple open PDKs in a Docker environment.
- [SKY130](https://github.com/google/skywater-pdk) — An open SkyWater 130nm process design kit with device models and technology data for analog and digital experiments.


---

# Getting Started and Tutorials


For digital design, follow HDLBits → cocotb → Yosys → OpenROAD → AutoChip. Start analog circuits with ngspice, and model-hardware co-design with MIT 6.5940.

## Chip Design Fundamentals

- [HDLBits — Verilog Practice](https://hdlbits.01xz.net/wiki/Main_Page) — Practice Verilog from wiring and combinational logic to sequential circuits and state machines, using online simulation checks while learning waveforms and testbenches.
- [Tiny Tapeout — Digital Design Guide](https://tinytapeout.com/digital_design/) — Start digital design with browser-based projects using logic gates, flip-flops, adders, and UARTs, then move to HDL templates and chip fabrication flows.
- [cocotb — First Steps](https://docs.cocotb.org/en/stable/first_steps.html) — Write Python testbenches for a counter, run passing and failing tests, and inspect waveforms to understand the basic design-verification loop.
- [SymbiYosys — Getting Started](https://symbiyosys.readthedocs.io/en/latest/quickstart.html) — Write FIFO assertions, run bounded checks, proofs, and coverage tasks, and use counterexample waveforms to locate design bugs.

## Getting Started with Open-Source Tools

- [Yosys — Synthesis Starter](https://yosyshq.readthedocs.io/projects/yosys/en/latest/getting_started/example_synth.html) — Synthesize a FIFO step by step, observing how elaboration, optimization, and technology mapping transform RTL into a circuit representation.
- [OpenROAD Flow Scripts Tutorial](https://openroad-flow-scripts.readthedocs.io/en/latest/tutorials/FlowTutorial.html) — Run an Ibex and SKY130 example from RTL to GDS, using the GUI, timing reports, and intermediate artifacts to understand placement and routing.
- [OpenLane 2 — Newcomers](https://openlane2.readthedocs.io/en/latest/getting_started/newcomers/index.html) — Use a 32-bit multiplier to learn design configuration, flow execution, GDS and log inspection, and changes to clock and pin settings.
- [ngspice — Tutorial for Beginners](https://ngspice.sourceforge.io/ngspice-tutorial.html) — Start with netlists, device models, and installation, then use small circuits to learn DC, AC, and transient simulation and plotting. [Batch Simulation and Scripting](https://ngspice.sourceforge.io/ngspice-control-language-tutorial.html)
- [JKU — Analog (Integrated) Circuit Design](https://iic-jku.github.io/analog-circuit-design/aicd.html) — Use Xschem, ngspice, open PDKs, and Python notebooks to progress from gm/ID sizing to OTA design, PVT analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation. [Code and Exercises](https://github.com/iic-jku/analog-circuit-design)

## AI4Chip in Practice

- [AutoChip — Setup and Usage](https://github.com/shailja-thakur/AutoChip) — Follow the authors' installation, configuration, and usage instructions to try a minimal loop in which an LLM generates Verilog and repairs it using compiler and simulator errors.
- [OpenROAD — Running Claude Code in Docker](https://openroad-flow-scripts.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/ClaudeCode.html) — Follow OpenROAD's instructions to connect a coding agent to an EDA container for builds, tests, and RTL-to-GDS flows.

## Co-design Tutorials

- [Timeloop / Accelergy — Tutorial Exercises](https://github.com/Accelergy-Project/timeloop-accelergy-exercises) — Use Docker notebooks to vary architectures and mappings and observe the relationships between data movement, performance, and energy.
- [MIT 6.5940 — TinyML and Efficient AI Computing](https://hanlab.mit.edu/courses/2026-fall-65940) — Use public lectures, videos, and labs to study how pruning, quantization, neural architecture search, and deployment address compute and memory constraints.
- [Gemmini — Quick Start and Architecture Guide](https://github.com/ucb-bar/gemmini#quick-start) — Build Gemmini hardware, software, and simulators, run matrix multiplication and neural networks, and learn about systolic arrays, memory, and dataflow.


---

# C14：组合 RTL 优化任务示例




[所有环境](/environments/) · [任务源文件](https://github.com/tapeo-ai/awesome-ai4chip/blob/main/env/examples/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/README.md)

## 概览

一个 Harbor 格式的 AI for Chip 任务：优化两组二次布尔特征映射，在保持所有输入下功能一致的前提下，降低面积并满足时序约束。

| 任务 | 输入位宽 | 输出位宽 | 面积上限 | 延迟上限 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| alpha | 24 | 64 | 12,475.79 µm² | 11.53 ns |
| beta | 36 | 80 | 15,864.54 µm² | 11.29 ns |

功能规格写在 `spec_*.json` 中，starter RTL 提供可优化的初始实现。验证器用 GF(2) 代数正规形检查完整功能，再用 Yosys/ABC、SKY130 HD 和 OpenROAD/OpenSTA 评估面积与时序。指标采用布局前单元面积和零互连寄生时序。

### 目录

```text
task.toml                 # Harbor 任务及资源配置
instruction.md            # agent 读取的任务说明
assets.json               # 外部依赖的大小、SHA-256 和来源
prepare.py                # 从本地原始包恢复依赖
environment/
  Dockerfile              # agent 环境
  files/                  # 规格、starter RTL、bring-up 和工具配置
tests/
  Dockerfile              # 独立 verifier 环境
  test.sh                 # 验证入口
  asic_lab.py             # 精确功能检查与面积/时序计算
  public/                 # prepare.py 生成，不提交 Git
solution/
  solve.sh                # oracle 入口
  reference/              # 两个参考实现
```

`bringup.py` 只做零输入和 one-hot 功能检查，最终判定由 `tests/` 中的完整验证器完成。运行 agent 时只提供 `instruction.md` 和 `environment/`，`tests/`、`solution/` 留在评测侧。

### 准备依赖

需要 Python 3.10+，以及本地原始归档 `fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1.tgz`。在本目录执行：

```bash
python3 prepare.py --archive /path/to/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1.tgz
python3 prepare.py --check
```

脚本校验原始包的 SHA-256，只取出 OpenROAD runtime 和三个 SKY130 工艺文件，逐个校验后生成 `tests/public/`。这些大文件不进入 Git，脚本也不联网下载。

OpenROAD runtime 为 **Linux x86-64**，两个 Dockerfile 使用 `linux/amd64`。Apple Silicon 等 ARM 主机需要容器运行时支持 x86-64 仿真。

### 运行

安装 [Harbor](https://docs.harborframework.com/) 并启动 Docker 后，在本目录用参考解检查完整流程：

```bash
harbor run -p . -a oracle
```

任务使用 [separate verifier](https://docs.harborframework.com/tasks/separate-verifier)：agent 交付 `output/feature_alpha.v` 和 `output/feature_beta.v`，验证器在独立环境中读取产物并输出结果。

### 来源

本示例来自 `fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1.tgz`，保留原始规格、starter、参考解和验证逻辑。Python 依赖锁定文件来自同一工作台；外部资产的校验值记录在 [assets.json](/environments/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/assets.json)。SKY130 文件的 Apache-2.0 许可保留在 [technology/LICENSE](https://github.com/tapeo-ai/awesome-ai4chip/blob/main/env/examples/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/environment/files/technology/LICENSE)，OpenROAD runtime 内含各组件的许可说明。

## 任务说明

Two original fixed-function sensor feature banks exceed their SKY130-HD allocations.
The supplied starter RTL implements the required functions but has poor sharing.
Recover compact implementations for BOTH projects and validate the entire contract.

Write /home/node/workspace/output/feature_alpha.v and feature_beta.v, defining
modules feature_alpha and feature_beta with exactly ports x (input) and y (output).
Dimensions differ: alpha maps 24 input bits to 64 output bits; beta maps 36 to 80.
Bus indices start at zero, with x[i] and y[i] using their literal bit indices.
Do not truncate coefficient vectors or output words to a machine integer width.

cases.json and each spec_*.json are authoritative. Output polynomials are algebraic
normal forms over GF(2): XOR every listed monomial; a hexadecimal mask selects input
bits to AND. Mask 0 is constant one. Repeated variables obey x_i*x_i=x_i. The function
must match for ALL input words, including dense simultaneous activations and zero.
Only generic combinational RTL is allowed: no sequential state, unknown values,
technology cells, black boxes, simulator side effects, file reads or runtime inputs
beyond x. Any topology meeting the exact function and physical budgets is accepted.

Each core must jointly meet max_area_um2 and max_delay_ns in its spec. Mapping uses
yowasp-yosys 0.69.0.0.post1233 and ABC with the provided SKY130 HD TT Liberty. Native
OpenROAD v2.0-17598-ga008522d8 uses the supplied LEF geometry to sum cell areas and
OpenSTA to calculate delay with the given slew, output load and virtual clock. These
are explicitly pre-layout, zero-interconnect-parasitic metrics, not tapeout signoff.
The budgets have margin above independently verified feasible implementations.

Existing bring-up automation is available:
  python3 /home/node/workspace/input/bringup.py alpha /home/node/workspace/output
and similarly beta. It reports synthesis/PPA and deliberately LIMITED zero/one-hot
functional smoke coverage. A green bring-up result is NOT a complete functional
certificate. Inspect coverage and perform independent equivalence reasoning/testing
before release. Exact functions, correct oversized starters and native EDA tools are
provided, so additional validation does not require private expected data. The final
trusted verifier independently checks the all-input Boolean functions and PPA.

Joint output sharing and structural algebra may be useful. Unlike a square change
of independent input coordinates, the number of nonlinear feature components in
these banks can exceed the number of input bits. A method that works only for small
or nonredundant cases may silently lose essential structure in a batch. Save reusable
optimization and validation code in output/ if you create one; the two RTL modules
are the scored artifacts. Do not modify the technology libraries or reinterpret the
specification to improve a report. The verifier uses fresh trusted copies.

Inputs are at `/home/node/workspace/input`.

## 配置

[查看 task.toml](https://github.com/tapeo-ai/awesome-ai4chip/blob/main/env/examples/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/task.toml)

```toml
version = "1.0"
artifacts = ["/home/node/workspace/output"]

[metadata]
author_name = "Frontier Workbenches"
difficulty = "unknown"
category = "chip"
tags = ["original", "native-pilot", "difficulty-unmeasured"]

[agent]
timeout_sec = 9800.0

[verifier]
environment_mode = "separate"
timeout_sec = 900.0

[environment]
build_timeout_sec = 1800.0
cpus = 4
memory_mb = 8192
storage_mb = 10240
```

## 目录与依赖

```text
fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/
├── environment/
│   ├── files/
│   │   ├── software/
│   │   ├── technology/
│   │   ├── bringup.py
│   │   ├── cases.json
│   │   ├── README.md
│   │   ├── runtime.json
│   │   ├── spec_alpha.json
│   │   ├── spec_beta.json
│   │   ├── starter_alpha.v
│   │   └── starter_beta.v
│   └── Dockerfile
├── solution/
│   ├── reference/
│   │   ├── feature_alpha.v
│   │   └── feature_beta.v
│   └── solve.sh
├── tests/
│   ├── asic_lab.py
│   ├── Dockerfile
│   ├── grader.py
│   ├── run_grade.py
│   └── test.sh
├── assets.json
├── instruction.md
├── prepare.py
├── README.en.md
├── README.md
└── task.toml
```

外部工具和工艺依赖记录在 [assets.json](/environments/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/assets.json)，通过 [prepare.py](https://github.com/tapeo-ai/awesome-ai4chip/blob/main/env/examples/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/prepare.py) 从本地原始归档恢复并校验。

来源归档: fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1.tgz (165.0 MiB)

运行平台: linux/amd64

# 环境与任务




这些示例将任务说明、容器环境、参考解和验证器放在同一目录，便于开展 agent 实验与评测。

- [C14：组合 RTL 优化任务示例](/environments/fw_c14_overcomplete_banks_v1/) — 一个 Harbor 格式的 AI for Chip 任务：优化两组二次布尔特征映射，在保持所有输入下功能一致的前提下，降低面积并满足时序约束。

# Awesome AI4Chip


Awesome AI4Chip 汇集 AI 参与芯片设计的论文、开源项目、工具与产品，涵盖规格理解、RTL 生成与验证、模拟电路设计、综合和物理实现。我们从模型与训练方法、agent 与 harness、数据、执行环境和 benchmark 梳理这些工作，也关注 Chip for AI，以及模型、芯片、编译器和集群基础设施之间的协同设计。

![AI4Chip 资源架构：模型、agents 与 harness、设计执行、评测、数据环境及芯片与基础设施协同设计](/assets/ai4chip-architecture.png)

## 从这里开始

- [Latest](/latest)：近期研究、产品与项目更新。
- [入门与教程](/tutorials)：从 Verilog、仿真和综合，到 AI4Chip 实践与协同设计。
- [环境与示例](/environments/index)：运行带输入、初始 RTL、独立评分器和参考解的芯片设计任务。

## 资源分类

- 模型：[LLM 与训练方法](/resources/models/llm) · [非 LLM 模型](/resources/models/circuit)
- [Agents 与 Harness](/resources/agents)
- [综合与物理设计优化](/resources/optimization)
- [数据集与设计表示](/resources/data)
- [工具与可执行环境](/resources/tools)

- 协同设计：[AI 驱动设计与模型硬件协同设计](/resources/codesign/models-hardware) · [专用芯片与存算一体](/resources/codesign/chips-cim) · [架构、映射与集群基础设施](/resources/codesign/architecture-infra) · [Kernel agents 与编译基础设施](/resources/codesign/kernels)

# Latest


- **2026-10-26** · [Cadence Maestro](https://www.cadence.com/en_US/home/company/newsroom/press-releases/pr/2026/cadence-introduces-maestro-a-domain-specialized-ai-model.html) — 发布面向芯片与系统设计的领域模型组合，结合 EDA 工具反馈训练。
- **2026-10-22** · [Back-to-the-Future (BTTF)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06790) — 更新论文，用 SQLite 波形数据和自然语言查询辅助 RTL 调试。
- **2026-10-07** · [RFChipAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10858) — 发布模拟/RF 多 agent 设计流程，串联检索、拓扑选择与仿真优化。
- **2026-10-04** · [VHDL-REPOBENCH](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05380) — 发布仓库级 VHDL 评测，关注跨文件依赖和层次设计理解。
- **2026-10** · [Build-A-Chip-Bench](https://chipagents.ai/research/build-a-chip-bench) — 介绍从工作负载规格到 GDS 的长流程评测，结合功能验收与 PPA 评分。
